hazards.name: Flooding and urban waterlogging
hazards.observation_period: KSDMA report published 2022; underlying historical-model reference period is not stated in the district summary.
hazards.record_coverage: Six official historical return-period scenario outputs; no dated district flood-event series or urban-waterlogging observations are included.
key_findings: KSDMA reports modeled historical-scenario affected area from 458.67 km² at the 10-year return period to 596.45 km² at the 500-year return period.
The report's return periods correspond to approximate annual exceedance probabilities of 10% to 0.2%; these are source-reported scenario statistics, not a forecast for a specific year or location.
The source-reported exposed hospital and school counts increase across the return-period scenarios; these counts depend on the source inventory and are not independently revalidated here.
hazards.seasonal_pattern_gap: The district report contains return-period scenarios, not dated events or monthly rainfall/flood observations, so a seasonal chart cannot be calculated.
hazards.method: Display only KSDMA's district-level historical scenario table and its source-reported return period/annual-exceedance labels. Do not fit or extrapolate a local model.
hazards.uncertainty: The reported figures are model outputs and depend on the source model, scenario definition, and exposure inventory. They do not estimate urban waterlogging frequency, ward-level impacts, or current conditions.

sources.title: KSDMA Flood Hazard Probability Report 2022 and Ernakulam historical map
sources.reuse_note: Official district-level published summary; the dashboard uses the source-reported historical-scenario table and does not sample the raster.

hazards.name: Cyclones and coastal storm impacts
hazards.observation_period: North Indian Ocean best-track archive is present; no verified Ernakulam impact period is available.
hazards.spatial_coverage: The available IBTrACS file covers North Indian Ocean storm tracks; no district-boundary intersection or impact dataset has been validated.
hazards.record_coverage: No verified Ernakulam track-impact/event count. The regional track file is not treated as an Ernakulam event series.
key_findings: A NOAA/NCEI IBTrACS North Indian Ocean track file exists in the project, but track positions alone do not establish landfall, local wind, storm surge, rainfall, damage, or district impact.
No verified Ernakulam-scale storm impact inventory or district-boundary track analysis is available, so local event frequency and seasonal patterns are not reported.
hazards.seasonal_pattern_gap: No Ernakulam-specific cyclone-impact labels or verified district-intersection results are available for a monthly or seasonal summary.
hazards.method: No local estimate is calculated. Regional best-track data are retained as source context only and are not converted into district impacts or probabilities.
hazards.uncertainty: Best-track completeness and positional uncertainty vary by storm and period. A track near a city reference point is not evidence of district-wide impact.

sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

hazards.name: Landslides
hazards.status: Historical report context; no usable local susceptibility overlay
hazards.observation_period: NASA catalog reports dated 17 August 2012 and 5 August 2013; GSI susceptibility layer listed as 2022 mapping.
hazards.spatial_coverage: KSDMA lists a GSI susceptibility layer for Ernakulam district; its project copy is not fit for spatial analysis.
hazards.record_coverage: Three NASA Global Landslide Catalog entries explicitly mention Ernakulam/Erakulam across two reported dates; two 2012 entries may describe the same episode. The catalog is not exhaustive. The three GSI susceptibility polygons (High, Moderate, Low) all fail geometry validity checks.
key_findings: The NASA Global Landslide Catalog contains reports naming Kadavoor/Erakulam in August 2012 and Cheeyappara, Ernakulam in August 2013.
These media-reported catalog entries are historical examples, not a complete event inventory or a frequency estimate.
The KSDMA-linked GSI layer contains High, Moderate, and Low classes, but all three polygons have self-intersections and cannot be used to assign a class to any selected local body.
hazards.seasonal_pattern_gap: The small, media-reported catalog sample is not complete enough to estimate seasonality or event frequency.
hazards.method: Show the dated source reports as historical examples only. Do not infer a rate, assign them to selector locations, or use the invalid GSI polygons for spatial classification.
hazards.uncertainty: Catalog coverage is reporting-biased; source coordinates have stated 1–5 km accuracy. The susceptibility geometry, legend, scale, currency, and reuse conditions need resolution with the provider.

hazards.name: Drought and water scarcity
hazards.observation_period: No usable Ernakulam drought observation period is present in the checkout.
hazards.spatial_coverage: No verified Ernakulam drought-index extraction, groundwater series, reservoir series, or drinking-water supply series is available locally.
hazards.record_coverage: Zero verified Ernakulam drought or water-scarcity records are available in the dashboard data.
key_findings: No district-scoped drought-index or water-scarcity time series is present in the current project data.
No Ernakulam groundwater, reservoir, drinking-water supply, or demand series is available to distinguish meteorological drought from water scarcity.
hazards.seasonal_pattern_gap: No local monthly drought or water-supply series is available to calculate seasonal conditions.
hazards.method: Do not estimate drought conditions from unrelated district or national data. Obtain a verified district drought index and water-supply/groundwater observations before rating.
hazards.uncertainty: There is no locally verified measure of meteorological drought, groundwater stress, reservoir status, or water-supply impacts.

sources.title: India Drought Monitor
